approach: Read each line's starting point directly from the graph, then use the slope from that start to the meeting point for each particle's velocity.

steps.text: Read the starting point of each line from the graph.
steps.equation: A starts at t = 0 s, x = 10 m; B starts at t = 4 s, x = 0 m

steps.text: Find the velocity of A as the slope from its start to the meeting point.
Find the velocity of B as the slope from its start to the meeting point.
The two lines cross at the point read directly from the graph, which is where the particles meet.

final_answer.value: (a) A starts at t = 0 s, x = 10 m; B starts at t = 4 s, x = 0 m. (b) vA = 2.5 m/s, vB = 7.5 m/s. (c) They meet at t = 8 s, x = 30 m.

common_mistakes.text: Finding the velocity of B using the slope from t = 0 instead of its actual start at t = 4 s gives 3.75 m/s instead of 7.5 m/s.
